title: Critical Minimax Risk for Complier Rank Effects with Root-n Complier Counts
banked_reason: Official D0.5 below field: tier=subfield, paper_score_ceiling 6.6 < 7.4, salvageable=false. Independent main validity confirms stop; math panel remains REVISE, with mean-mismatch rebutted by independent audit but no re-review, and accepted-bank comparison omitted. No Lean verification.
gap_reasons: The (L) kernel draws V_1 from intervals centered at A_nu_A, but then sets b^*=(q/A_n)V_1-√n X_1/4: at central totals its mean is q u_A-m_np_1/4, whereas the true B mean is q u_A (the true S_1=L_A+r_1 has the missing +m_np_1/2 shift). For any free margin coordinate p_{1,a}>0 this is an O(√n) count displacement, yielding nonvanishing TV rather than the asserted o(1) bound; projection to feasibility cannot supply the missing margin-dependent shift. Reconstruct a parameter-independent full-record kernel with the correct pooled-count law, then redo (L) and every downstream converse/transfer claim.

The flagship positioning does not compare its exact rare-complier rank-risk curve with the accepted-bank LATE-strength and transported-CACE frontier artifacts (stat_transported_late_strength_frontier and stat_transport_cace_roughnuisance_length); add theorem-level relevance and a precise distinction before claiming novelty relative to in-repository prior work.

The executed signal-one result remains a certified bracket, while the general evaluator and attaining sequence have no demonstrated practical runtime or finite-roster performance, limiting the advertised sample-size and estimator-choice use.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery attempted a uniform original-record reduction, certified Gaussian evaluator, total attainer, and matched strong-signal endpoint, and independently strengthened the signal-one Gaussian bracket to [4/25,2/11]. The official review halted below field with a formally REVISE mathematical panel; a fresh main audit found the mean-mismatch objection rebuttable through diffuse-window marginalization, but no panel re-review occurred. The accepted-bank theorem comparison and inaccessible Mao theorem comparison remain incomplete, and no Lean/F-stage verification exists.
tldr: The distinct-person complier rank effect has a single exact limiting minimax squared-risk curve under the stated balanced fixed-roster encouragement design and externally supplied exact type totals. The curve equals the certified-evaluable value of two independent Gaussian margin channels with observable background covariance indices. The proved record transfer gives a converse against every original-record procedure, and total deterministic rules using only public inputs attain the curve. At \(\lambda=1\), the improved certified bracket is \([4/25,2/11]\): an equal four-point margin prior gives the lower certificate, and the explicit clipped shrunk-product rule gives the upper certificate. The sharp strong-signal constant remains \(\lim_{\lambda\to\infty}\lambda^2R(\lambda)=11/12\).
gap: Regular rank-under-noncompliance estimation and direct-treatment finite-population projection do not, in the inspected sources, determine the unrestricted original-record minimax squared-risk profile when the latent complier count is proportional to \(\sqrt n\), conditional on externally specified exact aggregate type totals. This oracle benchmark isolates nonlinear margin contamination while holding denominator uncertainty fixed. Complete theorem coverage of the closest Mao article remains externally unverifiable.
fill: An information-preserving critical reduction, deterministic certified risk evaluation and total covariance-adaptive original-record attainment for one prescribed balanced design with public exact aggregate type totals. The numerical value and sharp endpoint belong to the same curve and calibrate estimator choice and precision across externally specified rare-compliance scenarios. Robustness to estimated or interval-known totals is a separate extension, not a result of this benchmark.
